semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Acoustic signal processing is inherently concerned with processing audio signals, making them semantically equivalent.
The term audio processing is broadly synonymous with acoustic signal processing, covering similar applications in processing sound waves.

parent_domains.justification: Acoustic signal processing is a subfield of signal processing, focusing specifically on handling sound signals.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Signal processing is the most general form that encompasses all kinds of specific signal processing, including acoustic, making it the closest parent domain.

child_domains.justification: This is a more specialized area within acoustic or audio signal processing that focuses specifically on handling and analyzing speech signals.

closest_child_domain.justification: Among the child domains, speech processing is the most directly related to acoustic processing as it deals specifically with one type of sound signal.

sibling_domains.justification: Though it focuses on biological signals, it shares the parent domain of signal processing, similar to acoustic signal processing.
This domain falls under signal processing but applies it to graph-like data, making it a sibling in terms of being a specialized application within the broader domain.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Biomedical signal processing, like acoustic signal processing, often deals with real-world signals that require advanced techniques for interpretation and analysis.
